findings.reason: the plan should cite `operator_request_body`/`run_operator_requests` as the existing owner of the one-call-site pattern and state whether `solve.fixed_point` extends/moves it or replaces it, instead of re-deriving the property from scratch.
findings.text: the design's §solve requires "Implement a fixed-capacity `lax.scan` state machine ... Active microsteps submit states and directions through the same `jax.jvp` call site ... The switch chooses a read authority" as if new, but `operator_request_body` (fixed_point.py:972) already builds one jitted primal/tangent body with a `jax.lax.switch` on `OperatorRequestKind` and both JVP members taken at the request's own state, and `run_operator_requests` (fixed_point.py:1026, `serve` at :1038) already serves a fixed-shape request stream through one traced `lax.scan` body without re-interpreting the caller's linear solve; the design's inventory row for `fixed_point.py` names only `_active_set_newton_krylov` and never mentions this reusable mechanism

findings.reason: the design already says `gs.apply` replaces rather than wraps `ForwardFluxOperator`, so the mechanism is inherited by construction; naming it would harden the clause but does not change the module design.
findings.text: the plan's §4 acceptance clause "one compiled program serves two geometries of the same shape, counted as compilations" relies on exact shape-based specialisation, which the design never attributes to a mechanism, yet `ForwardFluxOperator` (forward_operator.py:2321, `tree_flatten` at :2718) and the registered geometry pytrees (forward_operator.py:222–235, shapes carried in aux_data) already implement precisely that: numerical arrays as traced leaves with shapes in aux_data

findings.reason: the design must name `fixed_point.py`'s request machinery as the owner to move or extend (and say so in the retirement row), or the new solve will silently diverge from the tested single-call-site contract that `_operator_scores` and the one-map instrument already exercise.
findings.text: `solve.fixed_point` proposes to own the single traced map/booking/read body served by one `lax.scan` while the plan deletes `fixed_point.py`, so the mechanism has no named successor: either the plan duplicates it into a new `solve.py` or it deletes a mechanism it still needs, and neither is stated

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — each of the four proposed modules hides substantial behaviour (contour-tree read + sub-cell connectivity + clip for `topology.read`; connectivity-before-integration booking for `current.book`; the composed map plus its tangent for `gs.apply`; the scan-driven Newton state machine for `solve.fixed_point`) behind a four-argument signature and a typed result, and the design explicitly keeps geometry/polynomial/linalg helpers private rather than adding public surface.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — `solve.fixed_point`'s "one call site is a program property" design (design §solve) re-implements the exact pattern already owned by `fixed_point.py`'s `operator_request_body` / `run_operator_requests`, and the plan does not name that owner or say why it cannot be extended/moved.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the design's §1 inventory (17 null-role + 23 region-role source bindings) is a genuinely thorough prior-art search of topology, booking and map machinery, but it does not name the existing single-call-site request machinery in `fixed_point.py` that §5 re-derives, nor the shape-specialisation mechanism in `forward_operator.py` that §4's compile-count clause depends on.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — `current.book`, `gs.apply` and `solve.fixed_point` absorb their owners rather than forward to them (`gs.apply` is stated to replace the map `ForwardFluxOperator` performs "rather than wrapping it", §6), and the design line 34 forbids a second public booking or solver.
